cards.explanation: The answer is True. The Gazites surrounded the place and lay in wait for Samson at the city gate. They stayed quiet all night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.” (Judges 16:2) That's a heavy plan, and the text doesn't soften it. Hold on to it, friends, because it makes what Samson does at midnight hit even harder.

Samson pulls the gate right out, friends! He got up at midnight, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. (Judges 16:3) No lock, no latch, no problem. The Gazites were waiting quietly at that very gate, and I'd love to have seen their faces in the morning.

The lords want to know where his great strength comes from. They told Delilah, the woman Samson loved, to "…find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him…" (Judges 16:4-5) They weren't asking about his schedule or his hiding spots. They wanted the secret behind that strength, and they planned to use it against him.

The offer is silver from each of them, friends. Each lord promised Delilah eleven hundred shekels of silver. (Judges 16:5) That's from every single lord, not one pooled-up pot. The text names the silver and nothing else, so that's the whole offer.

The word is weak. Samson said that with seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, he would "…become as weak as any other man." (Judges 16:7) That's what he told Delilah. We'll see in a moment whether it was true.

He snaps the bowstrings, friends! Samson snapped them "…like a strand of yarn seared by a flame." (Judges 16:9) The men were hidden in the room, and nothing came of it. Delilah's first try was a flop.
The answer is False. The text says, "So the source of his strength remained unknown." (Judges 16:9) The bowstrings snapped, so they didn't subdue Samson. His answer hadn't given her the secret.

He snaps them off his arms. Delilah tied him up with new ropes and called out, and he snapped the ropes off his arms "…like they were threads." (Judges 16:12) The men were hidden in her room again, and again it did nothing. That's two tries, and two tries wasted.

The answer is weaving his braids into a loom, friends. Samson told her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man." (Judges 16:13) This one finally has something to do with his head. Notice how much closer it is to the truth than ropes and bowstrings.

The answer is True. Samson woke up from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web. (Judges 16:14) Delilah had called out, and he pulled it all out like it was nothing. That's three tries and three misses for her.

She presses him every day. The text says she "…pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death…" (Judges 16:16) Daily means every day, with no days off. I think that'd wear down anybody's patience.

He tells her his hair has never been cut, friends. Samson said, "My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb." (Judges 16:17) That's the real secret, at last. It's a heavy moment, because he finally told her all that was in his heart.

The word is strength. Samson said, "If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man." (Judges 16:17) That was the part Delilah had been after all along. Now she had the real answer.

The answer is False, friends. The text says Delilah realized he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, and she sent this message to the lords: “Come up once more…” (Judges 16:18) She wasn't unsure at all. This time she knew.

They bring the money they promised her. The text says the lords of the Philistines came to her, "…bringing the money in their hands." (Judges 16:18) That's the silver they had promised. They showed up with it ready.

What he doesn't know is that the LORD had departed from him, friends, and it's a heavy line. Samson thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But the text says, "…he did not know that the LORD had departed from him." (Judges 16:20) He was counting on the old way, and the old strength was gone.

The word is prison, and it's a sad scene. The Philistines brought Samson down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison. (Judges 16:21) He was the same man who carried off that city's gate. I think this one hurts to read.

The answer is True. The text says, "…the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved." (Judges 16:22) That's a small line, but it's there after a very dark scene. I'll leave it right there, friends, and let you wonder about it.
